$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=9,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=\left(\frac{1}{9}\right)\mathrm{d}u.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=9\left(0\right)+\left(0\right)=0\\ x=\frac{\pi}{9}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=9\left(\frac{\pi}{9}\right)+\left(0\right)=\pi.\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{9}} 9\sin\left(9 x\right)\,\mathrm{d}x\\ &=9\left(\frac{1}{9}\right)\int_{0}^{\pi} \sin\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=1\int_{0}^{\pi} \sin\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=1\left[-\cos\left(u\right)\right]_{0}^{\pi}\\ &=-1\left(\cos\left(\pi\right)-\cos\left(0\right)\right)\\ &=-1\left(\left(-1\right)-\left(1\right)\right)\\ &=2.\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{9}} 9\sin\left(9 x\right)\,\mathrm{d}x\\ &=9\left(\frac{1}{9}\right)\int_{0}^{\pi} \sin\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=1\int_{0}^{\pi} \sin\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=1\left[-\cos\left(u\right)\right]_{0}^{\pi}\\ &=-1\left(\cos\left(\pi\right)-\cos\left(0\right)\right)\\ &=-1\left(\left(-1\right)-\left(1\right)\right)\\ &=2.\end{aligned}

\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{4}{3},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Transform both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=- \frac{\pi}{16}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=\frac{4}{3}\left(- \frac{\pi}{16}\right)+\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=\frac{\pi}{4}\\ x=\frac{\pi}{4}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=\frac{4}{3}\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)+\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=\frac{2 \pi}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute and integrate:

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int_{- \frac{\pi}{16}}^{\frac{\pi}{4}} \frac{7}{3}\cos\left(\frac{4 x}{3} + \frac{\pi}{3}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x\\ &=\frac{7}{3}\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)\int_{\frac{\pi}{4}}^{\frac{2 \pi}{3}} \cos\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=\frac{7}{4}\int_{\frac{\pi}{4}}^{\frac{2 \pi}{3}} \cos\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=\frac{7}{4}\left[\sin\left(u\right)\right]_{\frac{\pi}{4}}^{\frac{2 \pi}{3}}\\ &=\frac{7}{4}\left(\sin\left(\frac{2 \pi}{3}\right)-\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\right)\\ &=\frac{7}{4}\left(\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)-\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)\right)\\ &=- \frac{7 \sqrt{2}}{8} + \frac{7 \sqrt{3}}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$
